literal: And separating (enemies), cherishing and securing (allies), and reuniting those who separated, is that which a ministry is capable of.
translation: A minister is one who is capable of dividing enemies, cherishing and securing allies, and winning back those who have parted ways.
modern: பகைவர்களைப் பிரிப்பதும், தன் பக்கமுள்ளவர்களைப் பேணிக் காத்துக் கொள்வதும், பிரிந்து சென்றவர்களை மீண்டும் சேர்த்துக் கொள்வதும் செய்ய வல்லவரே அமைச்சர் ஆவார்.
explanation: This couplet defines the core diplomatic duties of an able minister. First, a minister must know how to divide the allies of enemies (pirittal) to weaken them. Second, they must cherish and secure their own allies (pēṇik koḷal) to maintain strength. Third, they must be skilled at reconciling and bringing back those who have previously separated or defected (pirintārp poruttal). A true ministry is defined by the capability to perform these three strategic actions.
